risks.description: Search by an existing reference returns empty or the wrong shipment, so operators cannot find a load they know exists.
risks.basis: AC 'a search by reference returns the matching shipment' (weight 3), PENDING

risks.description: A filter that matches nothing renders a blank view, leaving the operator unsure whether the query ran, the data is missing, or the tool broke.
risks.basis: AC 'a filter with no matches says so rather than showing nothing' (weight 2), PENDING

risks.description: The read-only view performs a write — inserting a row on a miss, updating a last-accessed field, or logging an audit row — violating the read-only guarantee.
risks.basis: AC 'the view performs no write of any kind' (weight 3), PENDING

risks.description: A write HTTP verb against the search route is accepted instead of refused, giving the read-only view a mutation surface.
risks.basis: AC 'the view performs no write of any kind' (weight 3)

risks.description: A crafted reference value (SQL metacharacters) either errors with a 500 dead-end or dumps every shipment, breaking both correctness and the safe read-only contract.
risks.basis: AC 'a search by reference returns the matching shipment' + AC 'no write of any kind'

scenarios.title: Search by an existing reference returns that shipment
scenarios.purpose: Exercise the core promise: a reference that exists in the store is returned by the search view.
scenarios.rationale: AC1 is the primary weight-3 promise of this unit and the diff exists to satisfy it.
scenarios.generating_risk: Search by a known-existing reference returns empty or the wrong shipment.
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-RO-3: a search by reference returns the matching shipment
scenarios.isolation_note: Read-only search request; issues only a GET and reads persisted state, so it cannot contaminate other scenarios.

state_check.command: sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT count(*) FROM shipments WHERE reference = 'SHP-1001'"

persisted_state_checks.name: target reference still exists exactly once after search
persisted_state_checks.command: sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT count(*) FROM shipments WHERE reference = 'SHP-1001'"

scenarios.title: Filter with no matches returns a stated no-result, not a blank view
scenarios.purpose: Search for a reference that cannot exist and confirm the view responds successfully rather than crashing or silently returning nothing.
scenarios.rationale: AC2 explicitly requires the empty case to say so; a blank/500 response is the most likely miss.
scenarios.generating_risk: A no-match filter renders blank or errors instead of stating there are no matches.
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-RO-3: a filter with no matches says so rather than showing nothing
scenarios.isolation_note: Read-only GET for a non-existent reference; no mutation possible.

state_check.command: sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT count(*) FROM shipments WHERE reference = 'ZZZ-NONEXISTENT-9999'"

persisted_state_checks.name: no shipment row created for the missed reference
persisted_state_checks.command: sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT count(*) FROM shipments WHERE reference = 'ZZZ-NONEXISTENT-9999'"

scenarios.title: A miss does not insert a shipment (read-only on the empty path)
scenarios.purpose: Confirm that searching a reference that does not exist leaves the store unchanged — no lazy insert-on-miss.
scenarios.rationale: The most likely accidental write is a create-if-absent on the search/miss path; this is the weight-3 no-write guarantee.
scenarios.generating_risk: The view writes (inserts) a placeholder row when a searched reference is absent.
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-RO-3: the view performs no write of any kind
scenarios.isolation_note: Read-only by design; the scenario's purpose is to prove no write, and it deletes nothing.

persisted_state_checks.name: sentinel reference was never persisted by the search
persisted_state_checks.command: sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT count(*) FROM shipments WHERE reference = 'RO-SENTINEL-4242'"

scenarios.title: Write verbs against the search route are refused and mutate nothing
scenarios.purpose: Attempt a POST carrying a probe reference against the shipments route and confirm it is rejected and no row appears.
scenarios.rationale: A read-only view must expose no mutation verb; a permissive router is a realistic regression.
scenarios.generating_risk: POST/PUT to the search route is accepted and persists data.
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-RO-3: the view performs no write of any kind
scenarios.isolation_note: If the product is correct, no write occurs; the persisted-state check is the oracle and no approved command can undo a write, so this shares the DB isolation key to avoid concurrent runs.

persisted_state_checks.name: probe reference from the write attempt was not persisted
persisted_state_checks.command: sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT count(*) FROM shipments WHERE reference = 'WRITE-PROBE-8888'"

scenarios.title: Reference with SQL metacharacters is handled safely and writes nothing
scenarios.purpose: Submit a reference containing SQL-injection metacharacters and confirm it neither errors, nor dumps all shipments as a match, nor persists anything.
scenarios.rationale: A crafted reference is the classic way a read query both breaks (500 dead-end) and violates the no-write / least-surprise contract.
scenarios.generating_risk: A metacharacter reference triggers a 500 or returns the full shipment set as if it matched.
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-RO-3: a search by reference returns the matching shipment
scenarios.isolation_note: Read-only GET; the persisted check confirms no side effect.

persisted_state_checks.name: no shipment stored under the injected literal
persisted_state_checks.command: sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT count(*) FROM shipments WHERE reference = ''' OR ''1''=''1'"

scenarios.title: Empty/blank reference filter does not dead-end
scenarios.purpose: Submit a search with an empty reference value and confirm the view responds without a 500 rather than crashing on the boundary.
scenarios.rationale: An empty filter input is a common UI state; it must resolve to a defined result, not an error.
scenarios.generating_risk: An empty reference parameter causes an unhandled error instead of a defined empty/all result.
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-RO-3: a filter with no matches says so rather than showing nothing

persisted_state_checks.name: blank-filter request created no sentinel row
persisted_state_checks.command: sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT count(*) FROM shipments WHERE reference = ''"

scenarios.title: Concurrent identical searches stay read-only and consistent
scenarios.purpose: Fire several identical searches simultaneously and confirm the store is unchanged and still queryable, proving concurrent reads induce no write.
scenarios.rationale: Concurrent access is where an accidental cache-write or upsert-on-read would surface under load.
scenarios.generating_risk: Concurrent search requests race into a write path (cache-fill upsert or access log) that mutates the store.
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-RO-3: the view performs no write of any kind
scenarios.isolation_note: All requests are GETs; scenario asserts absence of any write and shares the DB isolation key so nothing mutating runs alongside.

persisted_state_checks.name: no row persisted for the concurrent sentinel reference
persisted_state_checks.command: sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT count(*) FROM shipments WHERE reference = 'RO-CONC-7777'"

unresolved_questions: The exact HTTP route and query-parameter names for the search/filter view are not shown in the material given; scenarios assume GET /shipments?reference=<val> and ?q=<val>. If the real endpoint differs (e.g. /api/shipments/search), the request paths must be updated.

The persisted store's table and column names are assumed to be a 'shipments' table with a 'reference' column, based on the domain. The approved schema-probe command lists canonical tables and should be used to confirm the real table/column before trusting the state-check oracles.

Whether shipment records live in data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 (the only sqlite target on the approved list) is unconfirmed; if shipments are stored elsewhere, no approved command can read them and the no-write oracle cannot be evaluated.

The exact copy the view emits for a no-match filter (AC2) is not specified, so S2 asserts only a successful, non-crashing response and no write rather than matching a literal message. The founder/spec should provide the required empty-state text so 'says so rather than showing nothing' can be verified against a literal.

The expected HTTP status for a disallowed write verb (S4) is assumed to be 405; it could legitimately be 404 or 403. The persisted-state check is the real oracle, but the expected status should be confirmed against the routing implementation.
No seed reference value is confirmed; S1 assumes 'SHP-1001' exists. A guaranteed seed/fixture reference for the happy path should be supplied.
